tagline: A compact, residential European side district with a strong local identity — well-connected by metro, extremely affordable, and far off the expat radar in the best possible way.

items.name: Güngören Lokantalari
items.description: Unpretentious lokanta restaurants in the district centre serving rotating daily menus of traditional Turkish food at rock-bottom prices.

items.name: Merter Börekçiler
items.description: The Merter border of Güngören has excellent börek and pastry shops popular with morning commuters.

items.name: Güngören Semt Pazarı
items.description: A lively weekly street market with fresh produce, clothing, and budget household goods. Very local and very busy.

items.name: Merkez Kafeler
items.description: Local tea houses and small cafés around the district centre — inexpensive and frequented by the neighbourhood's residents.

tips: Güngören has good metro connections (M1A at Merter) — Bakırköy and the city centre are accessible without a car.
One of the cheapest places to rent in Istanbul for a functional European side address.
Merter, right on its border, is worth knowing for budget clothing and fabric shopping.
Quiet and functional — good for long-term living if you value affordability over buzz.
